uncited: The method consists of an offline pre-processing stage (typically CPU-based) and an online rendering stage (GPU-based).
**Frequency Volume:** A 3D texture representing the complex-valued 3D FFT of the spatial volume.
**Interpolation Kernels:** 1D discretized kernels stored in textures.
**3D FFT:** Perform a 3D Fast Fourier Transform on the rearranged data.
The rendering stage is divided into Slicing and Inverse FFT.
Transform the resampled 2D slice back to the spatial domain.
*   **Vignetting Artifact:** Central values of the final image are overemphasized due to the frequency response of the interpolation filter.

*   **Limitations:** Requires hardware support for floating-point 3D textures (or workarounds for NVIDIA); sensitive to interpolation quality; vignetting and ghosting artifacts require careful handling.
Frequency Domain Volume Rendering was introduced as a hardware-accelerated technique to improve rendering performance for large volumetric datasets.
The method leverages the projection-slice theorem, where a projection in the spatial domain corresponds to a slice through the origin in the frequency domain.
